newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina proposes regional anti-guerrilla force.
newsitem.headline: Argentina proposes regional anti-guerrilla force.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said in a signed column on Saturday he will propose setting up a pan-American anti-terrorist and anti-drug force and regional courts to deal with cases of guerrilla attacks.
In an opinion column in the independent news agency DyN Menem said guerrilla attacks usually cross borders and require "an international commitment."
"That is why I have decided to invite the Organisation of American States (OAS) member countries to set up the Inter- American Forces of Democratic Consolidation," he said.

He also said attacks such as the recent storming of the Japanese ambassador's house in Peru where Marxist rebels held 72 hostages for more than four months before Peruvian forces stormed the building, killed the rebels and freed the captives should be handled by inter-American courts.
"Those sentenced would be housed in an extra-territorial prison which would have the necessary infrastructure and means to prevent any attempt at escape or oppression that might arise."
Menem did not spell out what kind of forces he had in mind, other than saying that they should have national police chapters with specially trained and equipped officers.
A government spokesman said he had no details on the proposal other than those printed in Menem's column, entitled "International terrorism."

In a passage likely to stir controversy in an area highly sensitive to foreign interventions, Menem said the new force could step in if the affected country requested help or when its own "collegiate board" so decided.

The Argentine leader said the corps he would propose to OAS partners should help prevent drug-trafficking, terrorism and money laundering. The OAS includes all countries in the Americas except Marxist Cuba, which was expelled 35 years ago.
Citing examples of bombings and toxic gas attacks in the United States, Japan, Spain and Algeria, Menem said "terrorism is one of the major problems affecting the world today."

He also mentioned the bombings in Buenos Aires of the Israeli embassy in 1992 and a Jewish community centre in 1994 in which more than 100 people were killed. The United States and Israel have accused Iranian-backed extremists for the bombings, but the attackers have not been found.
"Democracies in the Americas must be given the necessary elements to ensure not just peace but the consolidation of our system of government," Menem said.
